newsitem.title: USA: NBC head looks askance at free political airtime.
newsitem.headline: NBC head looks askance at free political airtime.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 24, Reuter - NBC President Robert Wright on Tuesday knocked down a proposal by a U.S. regulator that local television stations give free airtime to some non-presidential candidates, saying nightly five-minute talks by campaigners would be boring television.

"Everything in our bones tells us that vignettes by politicians .... That's not an attractive programming concept," Wright said after an appearance at an industry conference sponsored by Broadcasting & Cable magazine.
Wright said political candidates received extensive coverage on news programs produced by NBC, a unit of General Electric Co.

Earlier, Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt said television companies operating local stations should give free airtime to candidates for the Senate, House of Representatives and state governorships. He said he would work to win wide industry agreement on the proposal after the U.S. presidential election.

A.H. Belo Corp, a newspaper and televison company based in Texas, had agreed to give five-minute slots to Senate, House and gubernatorial candidates on its seven stations, Hundt said. The give-away to the non-presidential candidates was the first by a commerical station in the United States, an aide to Hundt said.

Hundt told reporters after a speech at the conference that he aimed to spur an industry discussion on his proposal, but did not believe regulations would be required to get wide adoption by the roughly 1,500 local television stations across the United States.

Peter Lund, chief executive of CBS Inc, the television network owned by Westinghouse Electric, said scheduling the scores of non-presidential candidates in many televison markets would be a logistical nightmare. Any changes in using television for elections should be part of overall campaign reform, he said.
Lund said he knew of no evidence that suggested giving free airtime to candidates would cut back in paid political advertising.

Political advertising is a major profit source for U.S. broadcasters, giving lifts to industry earnings especially during presidental elections held every four years. An extended debate on giving free time to presidential candidates was touched off earlier this year by an offer of free time from the Fox network owned by News Corp Ltd.
